key_insight: A simple online safety monitor can detect when an LLM’s outputs may no longer be safe by thresholding an external verifier signal. With risk-controlled calibration, this lightweight approach performs competitively in real-time safety monitoring tasks.
problem_solved: LLMs can still produce unsafe outputs after alignment, especially during deployment. This paper addresses how to monitor model outputs online and trigger an alarm before unsafe behavior becomes unacceptable.
method: Use an external verifier model to score each LLM output in real time.
Convert the verifier score into an alarm decision by applying a threshold.
Calibrate the threshold using risk control to keep safety monitoring reliable.
impact: This gives practitioners a practical, low-complexity way to add deployment-time safety monitoring to LLM systems. It can help detect unsafe generations early in high-stakes settings without requiring a complex monitoring pipeline.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing LLM output flowing into an external verifier and then into an alarm threshold.
Threshold chart illustrating safe vs unsafe regions and the calibrated decision boundary.
Comparison plot of monitor performance on mathematical reasoning and red teaming datasets.
Icon set for 'safe', 'warning', and 'alarm' states to show real-time monitoring behavior.
paper_authors: Mona Schirmer, Metod Jazbec, Alexander Timans, Christian Naesseth, Maja Waldron
